name: Dual wavetable voice with an interval-locked tune/detune pair and a per-oscillator 'animator' on position and level: Reese bass, phasing-in harmony, S&H atmos pad and level-ramp pluck recipes
goal: Patch a two-wavetable-oscillator voice in which tune transposes both oscillators while detune holds osc 2's interval (fifth, fourth, compound fifth, or a few cents). Each oscillator has its own modulator on WT position and on level (bipolar depth from the current position; one-shot envelope shapes or looping, tempo-synced LFO/S&H/random). Use it for four portable recipes: (1) a Reese bass with ~15 cents detune and opposite-direction position modulation; (2) a chord lead where osc 2 at −5 st fades in on a slow ramp-up level shape and brightens as it enters; (3) an atmospheric pad with tempo-synced sample-and-hold on both positions at different speeds, osc 2 at +19 st, and modulated S&H speed for generative bursts; (4) a pluck made from a looping ramp-down level shape. Delta vs our wavetable-crossfade and opposite-vector pads: interval locking plus per-osc level animators as the envelope.

source.title: Wavefinder Tutorial // Wavetable on Tonverk with OS 1.3.0
source.transcript_note: Groovebox OS feature tutorial; hardware button paths dropped, recipes mapped to generic dual-WT modules. Factory wavetable names omitted.

prerequisites: Two wavetable oscillators (Web Audio: PeriodicWave crossfades or an AudioWorklet WT osc, implementation note)
Per-oscillator modulators with envelope-like one-shot and tempo-synced looping shapes incl. S&H/random
Low-pass filter (as an effect), reverb send, overdrive

inputs.name: wavetables
inputs.description: Original/free tables: identical saws for Reese; saw + metallic FM; airy/hollow + noisy; noisy brightening layer

inputs.name: notes
inputs.description: Bass line, chords, or plucked pattern

outputs.name: dual_wt_patch
outputs.description: Reese bass, harmonised lead, atmospheric pad or WT pluck

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Tune moves both oscillators; detune offsets osc 2 only, so the interval survives transposition.
Position modulation depth is bipolar and starts from the current base position. Negative depth subtracts.
Too much position movement thins the low end of basses. Keep it subtle and slow there.
Values beyond those named (±15/±10 cents, −5/+7/+19 st) are by ear.

steps.action: Load a wavetable on each oscillator and balance them with the level controls. Set an interval with osc-2 detune (e.g. +7 st = fifth); transpose the pair with tune and confirm the interval stays.
steps.expect: Two blended WT oscillators; transposing keeps the interval

steps.action: Learn the per-osc animator: raise position depth to scan from the current base position on each note (negative depth scans backwards). Choose a one-shot envelope shape or a looping, tempo-synced LFO shape; set speed. The same animator can also drive level.
steps.expect: Position visibly moves on each note trigger

steps.action: Reese bass: identical saw tables, osc-2 detune ~15 cents (or ~10 for subtler beating), lower tune slightly to darken. Set both to similar start positions, then positive position depth on osc 1 and negative on osc 2 so they move in opposite directions, subtle depth, slow speed.
steps.expect: Thick beating bass with gentle opposing timbral motion and a solid low end

steps.action: Harmony lead: saw on osc 1 and a metallic FM-style table on osc 2, detune −5 st (fourth / inverted fifth). Put a ramp-up one-shot shape on osc 2's level at a slow speed so the harmony fades in. Scan the table first (this one gets brighter toward the end), start osc 2 partway in, and add positive position depth so it brightens as it enters. Osc 1 gets a slow, deep triangle loop on position plus a little level modulation from the same shape.
steps.expect: Chords bloom: harmony fades in and brightens rather than hitting at once

steps.action: Optionally layer the track LFO subtly on position, a subtle pitch-envelope bend, a low-pass filter effect with slow modulation, and a reverb send; sequence per-step changes of modulation speed/depth for rhythmic variation.

Atmospheric pad: airy/hollow table on osc 1, noisy/aggressive table on osc 2. Tempo-synced sample-and-hold on osc-1 position (jumps each step), faster; S&H on osc 2 at a slower speed (use the random/smooth shape instead for gentle drift). Detune osc 2 to +19 st (compound fifth) and lower its level with level modulation. Modulate osc-1 position depth and S&H speed so the steps alternate between slow subtle moves and busy bursts. Add the LP filter effect and reverb. Each chord note gets its own modulation.

Pluck: main sound on osc 2 with a looping ramp-down shape on level, medium speed, full depth and low base level for a quick decay. Set base position near the bright part with positive depth so each note starts from the softer tone (or the reverse for a bright attack); compensate lost energy with overdrive. Layer a noisy table on osc 1 with the same level shape and speed. Use a long amp decay/release for a delay-like trail, then reverb and an LFO on pan.
steps.expect: Plucky WT voice with trailing tails

steps.action: Texture variant: load a sample (vocal, field recording) in place of a wavetable and pitch it down a few octaves; the same tune/position/modulation tools give a glitchy texture.
steps.expect: Recognisable sample character with a glitchy, granular-like quality

verification: Transposing with tune leaves the osc-1/osc-2 interval unchanged.
Reese bass beats audibly; returning detune to 0 removes the beating.
In the harmony lead the second voice fades in and brightens over the note.
The S&H pad alternates between sparse and busy motion when its speed is modulated.
